claims: Pairing uses a serialized native lifecycle core with injected store and transport implementations; it does not retain a vault authority lock while blocking on the network.
Production transport is HTTPS-only, proxy-disabled, redirect-disabled and bounded; pending 32-byte secret, device, vault and origin remain native keyring material.
Claim is recoverable through authenticated status; status validates exact device, vault and photo_inference scope before writing the protected reading credential.
Disconnect confirms server revocation before keyring removal; local read/write/removal and network ambiguity retain UNKNOWN or local material rather than asserting disconnect.

Status and disconnect inspect both pending and active protected entries. A missing or malformed pending entry with a valid active vault credential is server-validated before recovery or revocation; inconsistent or unreadable material remains UNKNOWN and retains local credentials.

Prepare and claim fail closed whenever an active protected credential exists, and reject corrupt pending material even without an active entry; neither path can overwrite a prior bearer or create a second grant.
Selected-photo capability and dispatch use server-confirmed pairing on spawn_blocking before creating a reading intent, retaining existing reading fingerprint and revision fencing.

Synthetic core tests cover lost claim response, restart recovery, scope/device/vault mismatch, keyring read/write/removal failures, offline disconnect retention, idempotent confirmation, late-status/disconnect serialization, active-credential recovery/revocation, and prepare/claim refusal with active, absent, or malformed pending material.
